name: Is an interior wall in a one-story house automatically safe to remove?

mainEntity.name: Is an interior wall in a one-story house automatically safe to remove?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Do not assume a wall can be removed simply because the home is a single-story building. Roof loads, ceiling framing, beams, trusses, attic supports, and later additions can still make an interior wall important.

Context: Single-story homes may also have slab, crawlspace, or post-and-beam conditions that affect new support. The wall’s relationship to the roof and foundation matters more than the number of levels.

Key factors:
- Roof and ceiling framing direction
- Attic access and visible supports
- Foundation or slab conditions
- Additions and prior alterations

Practical guidance: Take photos from the attic and crawlspace if safely accessible, but do not disturb insulation or framing to investigate. Elite Remodeling & Design can incorporate those observations into a site review and broader remodeling plan.

One story reduces some complexity but does not remove the need for structural verification.
acceptedAnswer.description: No. A one-story wall may support roof framing, beams, or concentrated loads, and its replacement supports may depend on the slab, crawlspace, or foundation. Verify the complete load path before removal.
